learningObjectives: Explain the role of dependencies in Case management
Differentiate between the Case Dependency and Timer wait types
Distinguish between a deliberate Wait Step and a delay caused by awaiting user action

elements.description: An automation shape that deliberately pauses Case processing and resumes it when defined conditions are met. Two Wait types: Case Dependency and Timer. Added to a Process in the Case Life Cycle like any other automation Step.

elements.text: Think of the Wait Step as a red traffic light in the middle of your workflow — it deliberately stops the car (Case) until the condition changes (light turns green). Sitting in traffic waiting for a slow pedestrian to cross is NOT the same — that's a user-action delay, not a red light (Wait Step).

elements.caption: Case Dependency: parent Case waits for child Case status. Timer: Case waits for a time interval or specific date/time.

bulletPoints: Wait Step = deliberate pause in Case processing. Two types: Case Dependency and Timer.
Added to a Process in the Case Life Cycle as an automation shape.

elements.description: Pauses a PARENT Case until a child Case dependency resolves. Add the Wait Step to the parent; when reached, it pauses until the child reaches the specified status. Requires a hierarchical parent-child Case relationship.

Two valid triggers: 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved'. Configure whether to check the child's status at the moment the parent reaches the Wait Step, or only track status changes that occur after that point.
You can allow users to cancel the wait conditions and continue processing the parent Case without waiting for the child to resolve.

bulletPoints: Wait Step goes on the PARENT Case — not the child.
Configurable: check child's CURRENT status OR watch for FUTURE status changes.
Prerequisite: parent-child Case relationship must exist.
Users can optionally be allowed to cancel the wait and continue.

elements.description: Pauses a Case until a time condition is met. Two options: (1) Set date/time interval — pause for a fixed duration (e.g., 24 hours). (2) Reference date/time — pause until a specific date/time stored in a Case field is reached.

items: Fixed interval: pause 24 hours for photo upload before review
Reference date: pause until end-of-day for fund valuation
Regulatory: pause exactly 72 hours before final review

bulletPoints: Timer option 1: fixed interval — specific hours/minutes.
Timer option 2: reference date/time — pause until a date/time field value is reached.
Common use: waiting for time-based conditions (SLA windows, processing cutoffs, upload deadlines).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Wait Step vs. User Action Delay

elements.description: A Wait Step is a DELIBERATELY configured automation that pauses Case processing. A user action delay is when Case processing stalls because a user has not completed an Assignment — NOT a Wait Step. These are completely different concepts.

A Case that appears paused because a user hasn't acted on an Assignment or submitted required data. NOT a configured Wait Step — just the natural flow of waiting for human action. Examples: awaiting manager approval, or uploading photos.

bulletPoints: Wait Step = deliberate. Configured by SA as an automation shape in the Process.
User action delay = incidental. Case is waiting for a human to complete their Assignment.
Manager not approving = user action delay (NOT Wait Step).
User not submitting photos = user action delay (NOT Wait Step).

examPitfalls.title: Case Dependency Wait Step goes on the PARENT — not the child
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where the Case Dependency Wait Step is placed. Candidates say 'on the child case.' The Wait Step is placed on the PARENT case — it makes the parent wait until the child case reaches the specified status before continuing.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Wait Step is added to the PARENT Case. The parent pauses at the Wait Step and waits for the child Case to reach the specified status.

examPitfalls.title: Case Dependency requires a parent-child relationship
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether Case Dependency can be used between two unrelated cases. Candidates say yes. Case Dependency Wait Steps require a formal parent-child relationship — unrelated cases cannot use this mechanism.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A hierarchical parent-child Case relationship MUST exist. Case Dependency cannot be used between unrelated Cases.

examPitfalls.title: Child Case trigger statuses: ONLY 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which child case status values can trigger a Case Dependency Wait Step to complete. Candidates name specific statuses like 'Closed-Resolved.' Only two options are valid: 'To be resolved' (any open status) or 'Resolved' (any resolved status) — no custom status values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Only 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved' are valid statuses that trigger the parent Case to resume.

examPitfalls.title: Waiting for user action is NOT a Wait Step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes a case waiting for a user to complete an Assignment and asks which Wait type is used. Candidates say 'Wait for user action.' Waiting for user action is handled by an Assignment step, not a Wait Step — Wait Steps handle time delays and case dependencies.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A user action delay (manager hasn't approved, user hasn't submitted photos) is NOT a Wait Step — it's a Case waiting for a user to complete an Assignment. A Wait Step is a deliberate, configured automation shape.

examPitfalls.title: Timer has TWO configurations: interval OR reference date
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how many ways a Timer Wait Step can be configured. Candidates say one (fixed interval). A Timer Wait can be set as a fixed interval (e.g., 3 days from now) OR relative to a date property on the clipboard — both configurations are available.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Timer supports: (1) fixed interval (hours/minutes) and (2) reference date/time — pausing until a specific date/time field value is reached.

examPitfalls.title: Case Dependency can check current OR future child status
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether Case Dependency triggers only when the child reaches its final status. Candidates say yes. Case Dependency can monitor 'To be resolved' (which triggers while the child is still open) or 'Resolved' (triggers at closure) — both are valid trigger points.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: You can configure Case Dependency to check the child Case's current status at the moment the parent reaches the Wait Step, OR to watch only for status changes that occur afterward.

examPitfalls.title: Exactly TWO Wait types — no others
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how many Wait types are available. Candidates list three or more. There are exactly two Wait Step types in Pega: Timer (time-based) and Case Dependency (status-based) — no other Wait types exist.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: There are exactly two Wait types: Case Dependency and Timer. No others exist.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An auto insurance parent Case must pause until the 'Vehicle Damage' child Case is resolved. Which Wait type should the SA configure?

options.text: Case Dependency — pauses the parent Case until the child Case reaches a specified status
Timer — sets a fixed interval for the parent to wait before resuming
Condition — pauses the parent Case until a property value changes
Assignment — routes the parent Case to a manager to confirm child completion

practiceQuiz.hint: Waiting for a child Case status = Case Dependency.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case Dependency pauses a parent Case until a child Case reaches a specified status. Timer is time-based, not status-based. Condition and Assignment are not Wait types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring a Case Dependency Wait Step. Where should the Wait Step be added?

options.text: To the parent Case — the parent pauses and waits for the child Case
To the child Case — the child signals the parent when it resolves
To both Cases — both must have matching Wait Steps
To a separate monitoring flow rule that watches both Cases

practiceQuiz.hint: The Wait Step pauses the Case it's added to — which Case needs to pause?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Wait Step is added to the PARENT Case — the parent pauses at the Wait Step until the child Case's status condition is met. The child has no Wait Step for this purpose.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Case Dependency Wait Step is configured on a parent Case. Which child Case statuses can trigger the parent to resume?

options.text: 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved'
'Completed' or 'Closed'
'Approved' or 'Rejected'
Any status change on the child Case

practiceQuiz.hint: Only two specific child Case statuses are documented as valid Wait Step triggers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Case Dependency Wait Step in Pega resumes the parent Case when the child or linked Case reaches one of two specific statuses: 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved.' Other intuitive-sounding statuses — such as 'Completed,' 'Closed,' 'Approved,' and 'Rejected' — are not valid triggers for Case Dependency and will not release the Wait Step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA wants to use Case Dependency between two Cases that have no parent-child relationship. Is this possible?

options.text: No — Case Dependency requires a hierarchical parent-child relationship
Yes — Case Dependency works between any two Cases in the application
Yes — but only if both Cases are the same Case Type
No — but Timer can be used as a workaround for unrelated Cases

practiceQuiz.hint: A hierarchical parent-child Case relationship must exist before the Wait Step can be configured.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A parent-child hierarchical relationship MUST exist for Case Dependency. It cannot link unrelated Cases. D is an incorrect workaround — Timer waits for time, not another Case's status.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A regulatory compliance Case must pause for exactly 72 hours before final review. No other Cases are involved. Which Wait type is correct?

options.text: Timer — with a fixed interval of 72 hours
Case Dependency — pause until a review child Case reaches 'Resolved'
Case Dependency — configured with a 72-hour timeout on the child Case
Timer — with a reference date/time set to 72 hours from now

practiceQuiz.hint: Fixed time interval, no other Cases involved = Timer with fixed interval.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A 72-hour fixed pause with no child Case involved uses the Timer wait type with fixed interval. Case Dependency waits for child Case status, not a duration. D is less direct — reference date/time is for a specific date value in a field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A loan application Case must pause until the applicant's employment verification date — stored in a Case field — is reached. Which configuration is correct?

options.text: Timer — reference date/time pointing to the employment verification date field
Timer — fixed interval calculated manually to match the verification date
Case Dependency — wait for the verification child Case to reach 'Resolved'
Case Dependency — the verification date field automatically triggers resumption

practiceQuiz.hint: Pause until a specific date/time stored in a field = Timer reference date/time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When the resume trigger is a specific date/time stored in a Case field, use Timer with reference date/time. B calculates a fixed interval — this is less direct and error-prone. C and D incorrectly use Case Dependency for a time-based pause.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A manager has not yet approved an expense report. The Case is waiting. Which type of pause is this?

options.text: A user action delay — the Case is waiting for a user to complete an Assignment, not a Wait Step
A Case Dependency Wait Step waiting for the approval child Case
A Timer Wait Step enforcing the approval deadline
Both a user action delay AND a Case Dependency Wait Step simultaneously

practiceQuiz.hint: Waiting for a manager to complete their Assignment ≠ Wait Step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Case is waiting for a user to complete an Assignment (Approve/Reject Step). This is a normal user action delay, not a deliberately configured Wait Step. B, C, and D all misclassify this.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user has not yet submitted accident photos in the Create Stage of an auto claims Case. The Case is on hold. What type of pause is this?

options.text: A user action delay — the Case awaits completion of a 'Collect photos' Assignment Step
A Timer Wait Step pausing until the photo upload deadline
A Case Dependency Wait Step waiting for a photo review child Case
A guardrail violation — Cases cannot pause in the Create Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: The user hasn't completed their Assignment — that's not a Wait Step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Case is delayed because the user hasn't completed the 'Collect photos' Assignment — this is a user action delay. B, C, and D all incorrectly apply Wait Step logic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are valid Wait types for the Pega Platform Wait Step?

options.text: Case Dependency
Timer
User Action
Condition

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega documents exactly two types of Wait Step configurations — recall both.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case Dependency and Timer are the only two Wait types. User Action and Condition are not Wait types — they describe other concepts in Pega.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A child Case was already 'Resolved' before the parent Case reached the Wait Step. How can the SA ensure the parent Case still resumes automatically?

options.text: Configure the Case Dependency Wait Step to consider the child Case's CURRENT status — not just future changes
This is not possible — Case Dependency only watches for future status changes after the parent reaches the Wait Step
Add a second Wait Step to the child Case to re-signal the parent
Switch to a Timer Wait Step — it always evaluates current conditions

practiceQuiz.hint: Case Dependency has a configuration option for current vs. future status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Case Dependency Wait Step can be configured to check the child Case's current status at the moment the parent reaches it — covering the case where the child was already resolved. B is wrong. C and D are incorrect approaches.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the fundamental difference between a Wait Step and a user action delay?

options.text: A Wait Step is a deliberate process configuration; a user action delay occurs when a user has not completed an Assignment
A Wait Step is configured in Dev Studio; user action delays are configured in App Studio
Wait Steps require SLA configuration; user action delays are handled by escalation rules
Wait Steps are temporary and auto-resolve; user action delays are permanent until manually cleared

practiceQuiz.hint: Deliberate vs. incidental — intention is the key.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Wait Step is deliberately added to a Process to pause Case processing. A user action delay is incidental — the Case stalls because a user hasn't completed their Assignment. B, C, and D state incorrect distinctions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs a Case to pause for 30 minutes and then automatically resume. Which is the correct configuration?

options.text: Timer Wait Step with a fixed interval of 30 minutes
Case Dependency Wait Step configured to wait 30 minutes for child Case resolution
An SLA with a 30-minute goal that escalates and resumes the Case
A Condition Wait Step checking if 30 minutes have elapsed

practiceQuiz.hint: 30-minute fixed pause with no child Case = Timer with fixed interval.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A fixed time pause uses the Timer Wait Step with a fixed interval. B misuses Case Dependency (no child Case or status trigger here). C uses SLA/escalation which enforces deadlines, not pauses. D invents a non-existent 'Condition' Wait type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer asks about the Case Dependency Wait type. Which TWO statements correctly describe how a Case Dependency Wait works?

options.text: The Case pauses and waits until a specified related Case reaches a defined status or resolution condition
Case Dependency can be used to pause a parent Case until a child Case is resolved or reaches a target status
The Case Dependency Wait type uses a calendar timer to pause for a fixed number of hours or business days
Case Dependency requires an Integration Designer connector to poll the status of the dependent Case

practiceQuiz.hint: Case Dependency waits for another Case's status — not a time duration. Timer is the time-based Wait type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Case Dependency Wait type pauses processing until a specified related Case (typically a child Case) meets a defined status or resolution condition. This is distinct from the Timer Wait type, which pauses for a fixed calendar duration. Case Dependency does not use timers or require Integration Designer connectors — Pega monitors the related Case internally.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a Claims workflow where the Case must wait 5 business days before advancing to the Settlement Stage. Which TWO elements must be configured to implement this?

options.text: A Wait Step placed in the process before the Settlement Stage
The Timer wait type configured with a duration of 5 business days on the Wait Step
A Case Dependency wait type targeting the status of a related external Case
An SLA rule with a 5-day deadline and an escalation action to automatically advance the Case

practiceQuiz.hint: A time-based pause needs a Wait Step with the Timer type and the specific duration configured.
practiceQuiz.rationale: To pause a Case for a fixed time duration, the SA adds a Wait Step to the process and configures the Timer wait type with the desired duration (5 business days). Case Dependency is for status-based waits on a related Case, not time-based pauses.

quickRecap.value: Deliberate automation shape that pauses Case processing. Two types: Case Dependency and Timer.

Pauses PARENT Case until child Case reaches 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved'. Added to parent Case. Requires parent-child relationship. Configurable: check current status OR watch for future status changes.
Pauses Case for: (1) fixed interval (hours/min), OR (2) until a reference date/time field value is reached.

Wait Step = deliberate SA configuration. User action delay = Case waiting for user to complete an Assignment. These are DIFFERENT — manager not approving and user not submitting photos are NOT Wait Steps.
Parent-child hierarchical Case relationship MUST exist. Cannot use between unrelated Cases.
'To be resolved' or 'Resolved' — the only two statuses that trigger Case Dependency resumption.
You can allow users to cancel the wait conditions and continue processing without waiting for the child Case.
